Augment

awg-MENT -- stress on the second syllable, MENT. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To augment add to something to make it greater.

The hospital hired traveling nurses to augment its staff during the winter surge.

Worked Example

A weekend tutor, two library books, and a nightly practice quiz turn the student's shaky math grade into the strongest score on her report card.

Each addition augmented her preparation -- extra resources stacked on top of what she already had, making it greater. To augment is to add to something so that it grows in size, number, or strength.

How Augment Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

increase

increase: to make greater in size or number

supplement

supplement: to add extra to something

amplify

amplify: to make greater in strength or intensity

Antonyms

diminish

diminish: to make smaller or less

reduce

reduce: to bring down in size or amount

How Strong Is It? — supplement → augment → amplify

supplement vs. augment

supplement vs. augment: Supplement is more modest than augment -- a supplement tops something up with a little extra, while to augment is to build it up noticeably greater than before.

amplify vs. augment

amplify vs. augment: Amplify is more dramatic than augment: augmenting a sound system adds more speakers, while amplifying the sound cranks its very intensity until it fills the hall.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — aug-

root — aug-: to increase (Latin augere)

suffix — -ment

suffix — -ment: result or means of (Latin -mentum)

Put it together

Put it together: Augment comes from Latin augere, 'to increase' -- one of the great growth-roots of Latin. To augment something is simply to make it grow: you add to what already exists until it stands greater than before.

Root Check

Word Choice

Augment takes a direct object: you augment your income, your skills, your forces, your vocabulary. It implies building on something that already exists -- you cannot augment what is not there yet -- and it is the polished choice where 'add to' would sound plain.
